prerequisites: Archive core rowType is http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/Event and the extension rowType is http://rs.tdwg.org/eco/terms/Event (term-set detection: the 57-term set).
coreid resolves through ids.core-id-to-pk to exactly one emitted event_pk.
After removing byte-identical duplicate rows (count reported), exactly one Humboldt row remains for that coreid.
survey_pk = derived key with components ['survey-of', event_pk] (ids.derived-key-scheme; table 'survey').
survey.event_fk = event_pk. survey.surveyID stays empty: Humboldt has no survey identifier term, and eventID must not be copied into it.
Subject basis recorded as 'declared_row_type' (rowType eco:Event, dc:subject dwc:Event, coreid is the event's id), not merely core attachment.

Fields in survey that no Humboldt term feeds (surveyID, identifiedByID, samplingProtocol, samplingProtocol_fk, sampleSizeValue, sampleSizeUnit, samplingPerformedByID, samplingEffortProtocol_fk, informationWithheld, dataGeneralizations, feedbackURL) stay empty under this rule.
review_triggers: Two or more non-identical Humboldt rows for one event: no survey is emitted for that event until a reviewer chooses one survey per row (keys ['survey-of', event_pk, sorted IRI=value pairs]) or a single row; all rows stay preserved.

The event has a supplied eventCategory other than 'survey' (2026 Event core term): conflict, review. If eventCategory is empty, the core 'event-category' issue applies; 'survey' may be offered as the recommended option for events with a Humboldt row, but is not written automatically. dwc:eventType values (e.g. 'Survey') are not mapped to eventCategory by this audit.
coreid matches no core row: the Humboldt row is preserved and reported as orphaned; no event or survey is created.
evidence: back-end/api/templates/dwc-dp/table-schemas/survey.json: primaryKey survey_pk; event_fk required, foreignKey -> event.event_pk (predicate 'happened during'); weakPrimaryKey surveyID.

prerequisites_for_a_proposal: Core rowType is http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/Occurrence; coreid resolves to one occurrence.
The occurrence has a non-empty eventID, so its event is the grouped event ['eventID', eventID] (event.grain.group-by-eventID), not a synthesised one.

Every occurrence in the eventID group carries a Humboldt row and all those rows are byte-identical. The proposal is then one survey for the grouped event, with the same field and scope rules as on Event cores.
review_triggers: Always review: the extension declares an Event subject but is attached to occurrences; attachment alone does not establish that the occurrence's event is the surveyed event (gen-attachment-is-not-subject).
Rows differ within an eventID group: no proposal; conflict shown with the differing terms.
Only some occurrences in the group carry a Humboldt row: proposal shown with a coverage warning.
Occurrence has no eventID (synthesised event ['event-of', occurrence_pk]): no proposal; a one-occurrence survey would be invented structure. Preserve and report.

row_rules.rule: Each event with its own Humboldt row gets its own survey. No scope, flag or effort value is inherited, aggregated or propagated between parent and child surveys. Child events without a Humboldt row get no survey. The pinned survey table has no parent-survey field, so the hierarchy is visible only through event.parentEvent_fk.
evidence: sources/extension/f16a0de0c5bd-humboldt_2025-07-10.xml, targetTaxonomicScope comments: a parent event should 'include all taxonomic groups surveyed in the child dwc:Events' (a publisher obligation, not a converter inference).

row_rules.rule: occurrence.surveyTarget_fk (optional, FK -> survey-target.surveyTarget_pk) is never inferred from taxon names, life stages, the event link or the fixtures' excluded/non-target taxa. Only a reviewer decision may set it.

No occurrence (present or absent), identification, material, agent, protocol, bibliographic-resource, survey-protocol, survey-reference, survey-agent-role, survey-identifier or survey-assertion rows are created from any Humboldt term. absentTaxa/nonTargetTaxa/voucherInstitutions/samplingPerformedBy/identifiedBy/protocol* stay as strings on survey.
evidence: back-end/api/templates/dwc-dp/table-schemas/survey-protocol.json, survey-reference.json, survey-agent-role.json (agentRoleOrder required), survey-identifier.json, survey-assertion.json: none has a field whose dcterms:isVersionOf equals a Humboldt term IRI.

scope_rules.source_terms: All 14 scope terms (target*, excluded*, is*ScopeFullyReported), not only target*.
scope_rules.rule: Two or more populated dimensions. The reviewer chooses one combined target (conjunction of descriptors; the reviewer must supply the single isSurveyTargetFullyReported value, logged as a reviewer assertion) or separate targets per dimension (each needing its own valid flag; Habitat still has none). Until approval all scope values stay preserved and no survey-target rows are written.
reviewer_notes: Humboldt flags are per dimension. A true taxonomic flag alone may imply that the narrower conjunction (e.g. adult Lepidoptera) is fully reported, but Humboldt does not say whether the taxonomic flag was assessed independently of the life-stage scope, so this is not applied automatically.
A false flag on any dimension does not by itself establish the combined flag.

scope_rules.rule: A fully-reported flag whose dimension has no target*/excluded* value has no pinned field. Preserve it and report it. No survey-target is created.

catalogue_findings.finding: Says 'for Habitat (no such term) leave empty' for isSurveyTargetFullyReported. The pinned field is required (survey-target.json constraints {required:true}), so this produces an invalid package. The same failure occurs for any dimension whose flag is empty or invalid, which the rule does not handle.
catalogue_findings.fix: Habitat targets and any target with a missing/invalid flag go to review; never default the flag.

catalogue_findings.finding: All 43 terms are 'automatic', but 17 targets are typed: integer siteCount (minimum 1), abundanceCap (minimum 0); number geospatialScopeAreaValue, totalAreaSampledValue, eventDurationValue, samplingEffortValue (minimum 0); and 11 booleans. The XML declares no types, so values like '3.0', '40 m2' or 'yes' are legal DwC-A but fail ChatIPT's validator (dwc_dp_specs.py:426-456).
catalogue_findings.fix: Make these 17 conditional with the checks in the per-term entries; failures withhold the field for review. Strings stay automatic.

catalogue_findings.finding: No value/unit pairing, although the XML comments say each of the four *Value terms 'must have a corresponding' unit.
Only Event cores are covered. Humboldt on an Occurrence core then falls silently to generic preservation with no review item or explanation.
catalogue_findings.fix: Rule hum-row-occurrence-core (review, with a deterministic proposal only for identical rows on a grouped eventID).

catalogue_findings.finding: 'One survey per Humboldt row' creates duplicate surveys for repeated identical rows and silently creates several surveys for conflicting rows on one event.
catalogue_findings.fix: Collapse byte-identical duplicates (reported); conflicting rows go to review.

catalogue_findings.rule: hum-survey-row vs core-notes.md 'Survey. A survey is created only when the user opts in.'
catalogue_findings.finding: The extension catalogue creates surveys automatically, the core notes require opt-in, and neither covers event.eventCategory (required) for events carrying a Humboldt row.
catalogue_findings.fix: A Humboldt row is an explicit source signal for a survey row. eventCategory stays a core decision with a conflict trigger (hum-row-event-core). The root agent should reconcile the two documents.

catalogue_findings.finding: surveyTargetType 'degreeOfEstablishment' is not attested in the pinned examples. The schema example `establishmentMeans` is a different DwC term and must not be treated as an alias. 'taxon', 'habitat', 'lifeStage' and 'growthForm' are attested.
catalogue_findings.fix: Record a one-time policy for the label; until then the DegreeOfEstablishment dimension goes to review.

catalogue_findings.finding: No handling for exclusion-only scopes, duplicate elements, elements in both target and excluded lists, padding, or a byte-exact round-trip check.
A fully-reported flag with no scope values in its dimension has no stated disposition.
source_terms lists only the five target* terms, but excluded* terms also make a dimension populated, and flags take part in the decision.

'Same 57 terms ... no structural change' is correct for IRIs, required flags and thesauri. However, the definitions of dwc:identifiedBy and dwc:identificationReferences changed in the 2026 sandbox, the byte-identical sandbox copy c6866ebee757 is not listed, and filename dates differ from dc:issued.
survey.surveyID (weakPrimaryKey) is unaddressed; the derived key components for survey and survey-target are not in ids.derived-key-scheme.
catalogue_findings.fix: surveyID stays empty; keys ['survey-of', event_pk] and ['survey-target-of', survey_pk, dimension].

catalogue_findings.finding: No cross-field contradiction checks (e.g. isAbundanceCapReported=false with abundanceCap).

The 43 exact-IRI pairs are correct (each target's dcterms:isVersionOf equals the source qualName). The 14 scope terms have no exact-IRI field anywhere in the 79 tables. 'Never infer occurrence.surveyTarget_fk', 'do not mint *_fk from text' and 'hierarchy only via event.parentEvent_fk' are correct.

open_questions: Union semantics within one type: the pinned survey-target-descriptor documentation shows how include/exclude across types builds a scope ('all flying adult Aves except Passeriformes') but does not say that two `include` rows of the same type (Aves, Mammalia) form a union. This audit assumes union, which matches Humboldt's list semantics, and keeps one target per dimension so the per-dimension flag applies to the whole list.
GBIF boolean vocabulary (https://rs.gbif.org/vocabulary/basic/boolean.xml) is cited by 15 terms but not supplied; synonym normalisation (yes/no/1/0) therefore stays a review action.

survey has exact-IRI fields for Event-core terms dwc:samplingProtocol, dwc:sampleSizeValue and dwc:sampleSizeUnit, while core-notes.md routes them to protocol/event-assertion. When a survey exists, whether these values should also or instead go on survey is a root decision outside this audit. This audit copies none of them.
Whether Occurrence-core Humboldt should be offered at all, or only reported, is a product decision; this audit recommends review with proposals only for the identical-row grouped-event case.
The survey-target ID weak key (surveyTargetID) and surveyTargetDescription are left empty; a reviewer could supply a description, but none is derived.
